subject: URGENT: p99 & 502 surge after NeonV2 qprofile v4 rollout
messages:
From: Candescent Platform Ops <ops@candescent.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Anita Patel <anita@candescent.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden p99 spike + 502 rate after today's model switch

Hi Vivek —

We observed a large jump in p99 latency (from ~480ms to ~1.6s) and a rise in 502s across our production fleet starting at ~08:55 PT right after the NeonV2 qprofile v4 roll went live. This coincides with a scheduled switch from NeonV2 (qprofile v3) to v4 that was supposed to reduce tail latency. Instead throughput dropped and error rates increased.

Attached are a perf snapshot and a short sample of 502 responses. We rolled one zone back and saw partial improvement but it’s still much noisier than baseline. We need immediate help: impact is customer-facing (timeouts, retries).

What we need: a quick triage and either a rollback plan or an urgent mitigation path (fallback to v3, pinning, or traffic shaping). Please advise on next steps and ETA.

Thanks,
Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
Platform Lead, Candescent.ai

Attachments: perf_snapshot_20280731.zip, error_samples_502.txt

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Candescent Platform Ops <ops@candescent.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Jul 2028 09:29:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Sudden p99 spike + 502 rate after today's model switch

Sanjay — thanks for the quick heads-up and the attachments. I’ve looped in Marissa (CS lead) and Grace (runtime) to help triage.

Short plan:
- Grace/infra to check kernel selection and CPU/GPU saturation on the hosts that saw the highest 502s.
- If a clean rollback is fast, we will stage a targeted rollback for traffic >90th percentile routes and then expand.
- If rollback risks destabilizing other regions, we will apply a traffic-level fallback to NeonV2 qprofile v3 for Candescent’s canary batch.

Can you confirm: did you enable any custom prefix caching for this rollout and approx % of traffic that hit the new profile? Also paste a sample request id that saw a 502 so we can correlate.

I’ll standby for Grace’s findings. Vivek

From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Jul 2028 09:43:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Sudden p99 spike + 502 rate after today's model switch

Quick signal dump after initial look:
- GPU utilization on impacted hosts is normal (60-75%), but CPU steal on the serving nodes jumped under tail load — likely kernel-level stalls during attention kernel selection for longer-context inputs.
- KV cache hit-rate dropped ~12% for Candescent; their workload has a higher prefix variance than our quant tests.
- Error traces show an edge-case behind a specific instruction sequence that trips a fallback path in the runtime which currently returns 502s while retrying an alternate kernel.

Immediate mitigation options:
1) Targeted rollback to qprofile v3 for the customer (fast, low blast radius).
2) Apply server-side heuristic to force the alternate kernel path earlier (reduces 502s but raises p99 slightly).

Given customer impact, I recommend (1) unless CS prefers a softer fallback. I’m preparing a rollback bundle (neonv2_qprofile_v4.patch) with a runbook. ETA for staged rollback: 35–50 minutes.

-grace

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Candescent Platform Ops <ops@candescent.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Jul 2028 09:58:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Sudden p99 spike + 502 rate after today's model switch

Anita / Sanjay — apologies for the disruption. We will execute a targeted rollback to NeonV2 qprofile v3 for your production namespace; this will be staged to 10% and accelerated to 100% if signals stabilize. We will keep you updated every 15 minutes.

Action items for Redwood:
- Execute staged rollback now (Grace + infra).
- Provide live metrics dashboard and link (we’ll share shortly).
- Post-mortem within 72 hours with root cause and mitigation plan.

Anita — do you want us to open a formal executive thread after stabilization? We can loop in our Head of Product and our CTO for review.

Marissa
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference

From: Candescent Platform Ops <ops@candescent.ai>

Cc: Anita Patel <anita@candescent.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 Jul 2028 10:10:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Sudden p99 spike + 502 rate after today's model switch

Marissa — thanks. We approve the staged rollback. Sample request ids: req_20280731_cand_88112, req_20280731_cand_88113. No custom prefix caching for this rollout. Approximately 92% of requests hit the new qprofile v4 in the first 10 minutes.

We’ll watch the dashboard. Please confirm when you begin and when 100% rollback completes.

— Sanjay

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Candescent Platform Ops <ops@candescent.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Aug 2028 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-stabilization summary and next steps

Summary: rollback to NeonV2 qprofile v3 completed at 2028-08-03T16:30:00-07:00 for all Candescent namespaces. Full traffic returned to baseline over ~20 minutes; p99 and 502 rates back within typical thresholds.

Root cause (preliminary): an interaction between qprofile v4’s kernel selection heuristics and a rare long-prefix request pattern in Candescent’s workload that increases branching in the runtime. Under this branch the runtime attempted an experimental fallback kernel path that retries and returns transient 502s.

Next steps / commitments:
- Engineering to implement an immediate guardrail to prevent the experimental fallback path from returning 502s (INF-9482).
- Create a synthetic workload that reproduces Candescent’s prefix variance for future qprofile validation.
- Post-mortem with proposed fixes and a safer rollout policy for qprofile changes by 2028-08-06 COB.

We’ll share the post-mortem and the perf capture via the Drive link. Thanks everyone for the fast coordination — apologies again to the Candescent team for the customer impact.

Vivek
VP, Engineering Operations, Redwood Inference
